subject: turtle
pitch: A green sea turtle gliding through the water. A heart-shaped shell with olive and caramel plates traced in darker brown, a pale yellow belly plate, a blunt head with cream-edged scales, dark wise eyes and a gentle beak. Long front flippers spread wide, short rear flippers, and a little remora fish riding under its shell.
reasoning:
I'm sizing the turtle model, roughly a 1.1m shell and 0.9m width, and deciding whether its lowest points like flipper tips should rest at ground level even though it's meant to be gliding through water.

I'm planning the skeleton with a root joint at the body center and chains for neck, head, jaw, front and rear flippers, tail, and a remora. For the shell, I'm sweeping a heart-shaped carapace profile along its length with varying width and height to form the dome, then painting olive and caramel scute patches with brown gaps between them.

For the loft I'll sweep through stations along z using a single bone and centered catmull points, keeping the shell height around 0.3-0.47 with a rounded but fairly flat belly, skipping extra vertebral ridge detail for now. Next I'm moving on to shaping the head.

Adding white glints and tiny nostrils to the eyes, then plotting the front flipper joint chain from shoulder outward, back, and down with a sequence of positioned points.

For the flippers themselves, I'm weighing a flat sweep with asymmetric radius versus extruding a 2D outline per flipper with bone-based skinning for the joints, leaning toward sweeping along the joint chain with a smooth bone-skinned radius function for better bending at the root.

Setting up explicit up-vector frames so the flipper normal stays roughly upward along the curve, with rounded tips. For coloring I'll countershade an olive-brown mottled top blending into cream underside. I'll mirror the flippers by looping over left/right side and defining the front flipper's shoulder point as the starting coordinate.

Defining the front flipper joints from shoulder to wrist with a tapering width, parented to root; then adding shorter rear flipper spans and a small tapering tail sweep tucked below the shell's back edge.

Now I'm placing the remora fish underneath the shell, trying to work out its vertical position so its body loft stations sit close to the ground without leaving too large a gap from the shell's underside.

I need to ensure the lowest point touches zero, so I'll adjust the remora's position and attach it to the shell bottom via a flat sucker disc, tweaking the shell height to close the gap. With that geometry settled, I'll move on to positioning the flippers using a Y offset variable.

Now I'm lofting the remora body along the z-axis through tapering stations from head to tail, applying a dark grey-brown countershaded color scheme, and building the sucker disc as a flat ridged box with fine dark-and-light stripe detailing on top.

Pectoral fin outline shapes done, now setting up a joint for the remora's root attachment and noting it needs a "remora" bone assignment, plus planning a simple lower jaw box with its own joint.

Next I'm building the neck chain with "neck1" and "neck2" bones leading to a head tip joint, defining a 3-point path curving upward, then adding a jaw joint parented to the head. I'll give the neck a constant sweep radius with rounded caps, painted in a mottled olive-and-cream pattern.

For the head, I'm shaping a scaled sphere at the neck's end with a patchy cream-and-olive paint pattern, blending into a countershaded underside. Then I'm adding a small box for the upper beak near the front of the head, colored tan, plus a tiny downward-pointing cone for the hooked tip.

For the lower jaw I'm using a slightly smaller box offset below and behind the upper beak, in a lighter tan. The eyes are small dark spheres placed symmetrically with tiny white glint spheres offset toward the front-upper-outer direction, topped with flattened cream eyelid spheres. I'm skipping nostrils and extra shell ridge details for now, moving on to defining loft stations for the shell profile at a slightly raised height, listing out width and height values along the shell's length.

Still refining shell geometry...

I'm adjusting the vertical placement of the shell center so its bottom edge sits just above the remora disc, settling on a center height with a small overlap allowance. For coloring, I'm setting up a paint function that checks the surface normal to decide between belly, rim, and scute regions, applying a mottled pale yellow pattern on the belly and a cream-ish tone for the rim, while importing helper functions like paint, patches, mottle, and countershade. I'm also identifying where the shell's silhouette is widest, around the middle where the normal's y-component is near zero, to properly size the rim band.

Now I'm defining the flipper geometry as a swept chain with a radius function controlling width and thickness along its length, tuning the math so the flipper tapers smoothly without going negative or flaring too wide near the tip, and naming the joint chains for left and right limbs so they can be parented to the nearest body joint based on spatial distance.
